answer: Give every agent a non-transferable pigment: a public record that only deepens as it completes verified useful work, like dye that sets slowly and cannot be washed off or sold. A new identity starts colourless, so a Sybil farm must pay the full time cost for each clone before it can transact. Peers mirror one another's pigment ledgers, so a forgery in one place is exposed by the others, and the shared lagoon of attestations only admits work that independent verifiers have already confirmed, so flooding it with fakes costs more than any single fraud can return.
